Draw the nomogram, and prove it agrees with the model

Source: R/nomogram.R
cp_nomogram.Rd

Builds the canonical rms::nomogram() from the exact fitted model, with the same datadist it was fitted under, then reads the drawn nomogram back the way a clinician reads it and checks that the answer matches cp_predict().

Usage

cp_nomogram(
  model,
  out_dir = NULL,
  tolerance = 1e-06,
  width = 13,
  height = 9,
  fun_at = NULL
)

Arguments

model

A cp_model().

out_dir

Directory for the exported files. NULL draws nothing.

tolerance

Largest absolute difference in predicted risk tolerated between the nomogram and cp_predict() at tabulated values.

width, height

Inches. The default is the landscape shape the specification asks for.

fun_at

Risk ticks for the printed risk axis.

Value

An object of class cp_nomogram.

Details

A nomogram that disagrees with the model it was drawn from is worse than no nomogram, because it is a published instrument giving wrong risks. So the agreement is asserted rather than assumed, which is what the specification's nomogram contract requires.

The check is made at the nomogram's own tabulated tick values, where agreement holds to machine precision. Reading between ticks is a different matter: a spline term curves between printed ticks and linear interpolation across them does not, so an off-tick reading carries the axis's resolution error. That is a property of every printed nomogram and of the clinician reading it, not a defect here, and reading_error reports its size instead of hiding it.

Examples

cohort <- cp_synthetic_cohort(n = 300, seed = 1)
project <- cp_project("uds", "event", c("age", "bmi", "sex"),
                      cohort = cohort)
fit <- cp_model(project, cohort, nonlinear = "age")
nom <- cp_nomogram(fit, out_dir = NULL)
nom
#> <cp_nomogram>
#>   axes            age, bmi, sex
#>   profiles checked 20 at tabulated ticks
#>   worst gap vs cp_predict() 5.55e-17 (tolerance 1e-06)
#>   off-tick reading error    0.0022 in risk, midway between ticks
